g.text: Ours: what Orchestra owns and runs
Interface: where work crosses, and my outbox

g.title: Someone asks me for a simple task; more asks when requesters trust me to deliver. — crosses: slack/jira in
Confidence fades on its own, faster while bugs are open, and faster when asks sit in my backlog.
research + ticket — crosses: read: jira, docs, slack, code
approve ticket — crosses: jira write (via outbox)
An implementation attempt with tests. Slower where the debt is high.
Failures and late findings leave lessons, and successes leave patterns worth keeping, unless the backlog is long and nobody stops to write them down.
The agents turn lessons into policies, docs, skills and tools for themselves.
About six weeks' half-life, faster when much is landing in the area.
Every landing adds some debt; flawed ones add more; a good playbook adds less.
Agents pay debt down when they have time; under load this is the first thing squeezed.
Company checks and the AI reviewer catch about 40% of flaws.
Company checks and the AI reviewer catch about 40% of flaws.
crosses: read: threads; github push; replies via outbox
Approved with the flaw still in it; it lands, and surfaces later.
crosses: read: SAIL logs; github label
Trust erodes slowly on its own, and sharply when flaws are found late or bugs appear.
About 2.4 a week to start, rising to about 7 as the company's systems grow; fewer as preventions take hold. — crosses: slack/jira in
Monthly deploys bring the repeats back.
A repeat nobody filed comes back as a surprise.
Faster where runbooks already cover the command. — crosses: read: runbooks, code, docs
crosses: read: jira approvals, change tickets, org chart
crosses: slack write (the question back, via outbox)
root cause + context — crosses: read: customer jira, flag history, deploys, release calendars
root cause + context — crosses: read: customer jira, flag history, deploys, release calendars
run (me only) — crosses: bastion host (human only)
About 6% of commands cause an incident at today's runbook coverage; more when thinner, fewer as they improve.
crosses: read: slack, pagerduty, deploys, flags
log for the company — crosses: jira/slack write (via outbox)
Filed repeats come back as planned work; preventions automate some of them away.
A problem statement needs several cases; the more on file, the more often a pattern appears.
propose — crosses: docs write; slack post for review
Faster with more evidence on file, and much faster right after an incident.
People find ways around policies; automation drifts.
About two new projects, tickets or threads a week.
Slow where sources are out of date: the agent has to reconstruct what happened. — crosses: read: jira, docs, slack
When a refresh finds a source out of date, its owner gets a nudge; more often when hygiene is poor. — crosses: slack write (via outbox; earned autonomy)
A few nudges are fine; many wear patience out much faster.
Four a week at middling confidence; fewer when confident, many more after surprises. — crosses: slack/meeting in
1.5 hours of research when everything is stale; minutes when the page is current. — crosses: slack write
Each surprise is remembered while it is handled, and for weeks after.
Six to eight a week; the share with a real defect falls as the team's skill rises. — crosses: github in
crosses: read: PR, code, git log
crosses: read: PR, code, git log
Style and naming comments; more under a comment quota. — crosses: github write (comments)
Reviews given build goodwill, more when they come quickly.
How much other teams expect me to deliver. It brings asks, grows with landings, falls with bugs.
Researched and written up; waiting for my approval.
Ready for an implementation attempt: new tickets, diagnosed failures, bugs coming back.
An attempt finished; its outcome is decided by the playbook and the debt.
Looks done, tests pass, but has a defect nobody has seen yet.
Visibly failed attempts, flaws I caught, and flaws reviewers caught: to be diagnosed.
Policies, docs, skills and tools the agents use for this class of task, written by the agents from lessons.
Shortcuts in the code the agents work in.
Decides how much of the agents' work I check myself.
Change requests on sound PRs: style, naming, small asks. A fix round, not a flaw.
A real flaw found by company checks or reviewers. It costs trust and teaches a lesson.
Landed in about the last two weeks: the code churn that ages the playbook, and the evidence that builds trust and reputation.
Landed and out of the recent window.
Share of requesters who bring the change ticket and approvals with the ask, out of 100.
What the command does, runbooks, blast radius, risks, how to undo it.
Asked back for the change ticket or approvals.
Root cause and context: customer ticket, unsafe ramp, rollout follow-up, other environments.
Logged requests that are evidence for prevention, until they are too old to matter.
Policies and automation that remove the need for these requests.
How much of what gets asked is covered by an accurate runbook.
Repeats needed in government and monthly-deployed environments.
Repeats that will come back as requests when the next monthly deploy lands.
Something changed in the ticket, doc or thread since the page last read it.
How well owners keep their tickets and docs current, out of 100.
How often teammates' PRs arrive without real defects.
I have reviewed it; whether I caught the defect depends on the brief and my queue.
What the brief writer knows about the code: owners, risky areas, past bugs, conventions.
